findings.title: Strategy close() permanently shuts down the shared queue pool
findings.body: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` (and `join()`, which calls it) calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`. In `ResultsStrategyFactory.create_thread_queue_parallel_worker`, the same `self.queue_pool` is passed to every strategy the factory creates. StreamProcessor creates a new strategy on each partition assignment and closes the old one on rebalance. The first close therefore shuts down all queues and workers for the factory. Every later `create_with_partitions` returns a strategy whose `submit` puts into a shut-down queue, so messages fail or are never processed. Pool lifetime should be owned by the factory, not by an individual strategy.

findings.title: Kafka commit function is invoked from a background thread
findings.body: `_commit_loop` runs on its own daemon thread and calls `self.commit_function(committable)`, which invokes arroyo's `commit` callback. Arroyo's consumer is not thread-safe and expects commits to happen on the StreamProcessor thread that also polls. Calling commit from this thread can race with poll/assign/close on the same KafkaConsumer, and can produce undefined behaviour or errors during rebalances. Commits should be requested from the main processing thread, for example in `poll()` or `submit()`.

findings.title: A missing offset permanently stalls commits for the partition
findings.body: In `get_committable_offsets`, the loop breaks at the first offset in the range that is absent from `all_offsets`. Kafka offsets are not contiguous in general: log compaction, transaction control markers and deleted records all create gaps. If a gap sits at `last_committed + 1`, nothing past it is ever committed again, so the committed offset stops advancing and consumer lag grows without bound. After a restart, every message after the gap is reprocessed. The gap case should be treated as already complete, for example by skipping offsets that were never added, rather than as a blocker.

findings.title: Queues are unbounded, so the claimed backpressure does not exist
findings.body: Each per-queue `queue.Queue()` is created without a `maxsize`. Offsets are committed and the consumer keeps polling regardless of how far processing lags, so a slow downstream grows these queues without limit and memory use grows with it. The `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` docstring (around line 254) says the design provides 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', which is false for unbounded queues. Either bound the queues so `put` blocks, or fix the docstring and document the memory risk.

findings.title: Racy assertion that total_items is nonzero right after submission
findings.body: `test_stats_reporting` submits 10 items and then immediately asserts `stats["total_items"] > 0`. Worker threads may already have drained the queues by then, especially on a fast machine, so the test can fail intermittently. The assertion should be removed or the processing should be blocked until stats are checked.

findings.title: Error-handling test's assertion contradicts its docstring
findings.body: The docstring says errors in processing must not block offset commits for other messages. The test then asserts `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`, which requires that no commit happens at all. The worker catches the exception and still completes offset 100, and offset 101 completes too, so a commit for the partition is expected. The `or` makes the assertion pass whenever nothing is committed, so the test cannot detect the behaviour it claims to verify. The assertion should expect the committed offset to advance past 101.

findings.title: Offset-gap test codifies the permanent-stall behaviour
findings.body: `test_offset_gaps_block_commits` treats a never-seen offset (101) as a permanent blocker and asserts the commit stays at 100 until that offset arrives. This locks in the stall problem noted for `get_committable_offsets` and gives no coverage for gaps that will never be filled, such as compaction or transaction markers.

findings.title: Graceful-shutdown test asserts almost nothing
findings.body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_graceful_shutdown` sends five results and then only asserts that `factory.queue_pool` is None. It does not wait for or check that the queued items were processed or that workers exited, so it would pass even if shutdown dropped in-flight work. Similarly, `test_thread_queue_parallel_concurrent_subscriptions` is named for concurrency but does not check any concurrent execution.

findings.title: Transaction name hardcodes a 'monitors.' prefix in a generic module
findings.body: The worker transaction is named `monitors.{identifier}.worker_{id}`. This module is shared remote-subscription infrastructure, not monitors code, so the 'monitors.' prefix will misattribute uptime or other consumers' traces in Sentry performance data.
